newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone Rachel downgraded, passes over coast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone Rachel downgraded, passes over coast.

text.p: Cyclone Rachel had been downgraded to a category two cyclone and was now threatening the inland Pilbara region in the north-west of Western Australia, the Bureau of Meteorology said on Wednesday.

The cyclone was classified as category three on Tuesday, when it forced the temporary closure of offshore oilfields lying in its path and caused damage in the coastal town of Port Hedland. A category three cyclone can carry wind gusts of more than 200 kilometres per hour. The Bureau said at 3.00 a.m. (2000 GMT) Rachel had destructive winds of up to 140 km per hour but this strength was expected to ease in the next 12 hours.
The Bureau said heavy rain was likely to cause flooding in parts of the Pilbara region.
It said the warning was current for the Pilbara region between Millstream and Marble Bar, and south to Paraburdoo and Newman including Wittenoom and Munjina.
